title: Acceptance-Controlled MIS-PO: Adaptive Trajectory Filtering for Stable Off-Policy RLVR Training

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to identify what drives stability in off-policy RLVR trajectory filtering under high staleness. Paper [8] ("Prosperity before Collapse: How Far Can Off-Policy RL Reach with Stale Data on LLMs?") explicitly addresses the challenge of off-policy RL under high staleness, revisiting the issue of stability and performance degradation. While it does not isolate trajectory filtering bound magnitudes as the driver, it does investigate stability under staleness, which is substantively equivalent at the problem-class level. Quote: "their effectiveness hinges on tolerating large staleness in rollout data, a setting where existing methods either degrade in performance or collapse."

### Mechanism
The contribution's mechanism involves ablation of trajectory filtering bound magnitudes in MIS-PO, isolating bound tightness from adaptive control. None of the prior papers explicitly perform ablation targeting trajectory filtering bound magnitudes or isolate bound tightness as a driver of stability. Papers such as [8] and [7] discuss stability in off-policy RL, but neither isolates bound tightness nor performs ablation experiments specific to trajectory filtering bounds. No substantive equivalence is found.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves measuring the improvement (+12.76 percentage points) from tighter trajectory bounds in MIS-PO. Paper [8] uses a similar evaluation design, as it measures performance improvements under staleness conditions in off-policy RL for LLMs. While the specific benchmark instance differs, the evaluation design — assessing performance improvements under staleness conditions — is substantively equivalent. Quote: "we revisit this challenge and uncover conditions under which asynchronous RL systems can tolerate large staleness without collapsing."

### Domain
The domain is off-policy RLVR training of LLMs. Paper [8] explicitly operates in the same domain, focusing on off-policy RL for LLM reasoning under staleness. Quote: "Reinforcement learning has been central to recent advances in large language model reasoning." Other papers ([1], [4], [7]) address off-policy RL but not specifically for LLMs, making [8] the closest match.

**PURPOSE: Remove manual tuning of trajectory filtering bounds across staleness levels and training stages.**

The purpose is to eliminate manual hyperparameter tuning of filtering/clipping bounds in an RL training context. Paper [26] (AutoClip) explicitly states "requires hand selection of a clipping threshold hyperparameter" and proposes automatic adaptive selection. Paper [15] addresses "fixed clipping bound setting may limit performance of PPO" and proposes dynamic adjustment. Paper [21] addresses "selection of an appropriate step size remains one of the most computationally expensive aspects" and proposes parameter-free adaptation. These all share the objective of removing manual tuning of bound/threshold parameters in training. Paper [26] is the closest: "automatically and adaptively choosing a gradient clipping threshold" — same objective class (auto-tune a clipping/filtering bound), different host system.

**MECHANISM: AC-MIS-PO uses quantile estimation with exponential moving average smoothing to target a pre-specified acceptance rate schedule, setting bound magnitudes automatically.**

The core primitive is: track a quantile of a running distribution using EMA, then use that quantile estimate to set a threshold that achieves a target acceptance/pass rate. Paper [30] presents "a lightweight quantile estimator using a generalized form of the EWA" for "tracking quantiles of dynamically varying data stream distributions" — this is exactly the quantile-via-EMA primitive. Paper [14] proposes "step-size adaptation methods" targeting "a desired acceptance rate" using a filter on acceptance indicators — same acceptance-rate-targeting primitive. Paper [17] shows "it is not difficult for an algorithm to tune these step sizes automatically to obtain a desired acceptance probability" in MCMC. The combination of quantile-EMA estimation ([30]) + acceptance-rate targeting ([14],[17]) covers the mechanism. Paper [30] covers the quantile-EMA primitive directly.

**EVALUATION: Controller discovers appropriate bounds automatically while maintaining stable training under staleness s=256, where Fixed MIS-PO crashed at step 94 from gradient explosion.**

The evaluation design is: compare adaptive vs. fixed bound/threshold under stress conditions (high staleness), measuring training stability (crash vs. no crash). Paper [26] (AutoClip) evaluates adaptive vs. fixed gradient clipping thresholds measuring training stability/generalization. Paper [15] evaluates dynamic vs. fixed clipping bounds in PPO training. Paper [7] evaluates off-policy LLM training stability under staleness. These use the same design: adaptive-vs-fixed threshold comparison measuring training stability — a named comparison protocol. The specific object (MIS-PO at s=256) is a parameter change, not a design change.

**DOMAIN: Off-policy RLVR training of LLMs.**

Paper [7] (VESPO) explicitly addresses "off-policy updates... in reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs) due to rollout staleness from asynchronous training." This is the same domain.
